seasonUncovered: If the Earth had a −45° axial tilt at this position in its orbit, the axis would be perpendicular to the Sun’s rays, causing both hemispheres to receive sunlight at nearly similar angles, with direct sunlight concentrated at the Equator. This equinox-like configuration would create transitional conditions in which the Northern Hemisphere would rapidly cool as it shifted from summer toward autumn, while the Southern Hemisphere would rapidly warm as it transitioned from winter toward spring. The exaggerated −45° tilt would amplify seasonal contrasts and hasten these transitions, producing more dramatic temperature shifts between seasons.
